plain_text_guidance: Buyer-owned planning sheet. All buyer values and status cells start blank. Enter your own values only; this file contains no supplier prices or productivity benchmarks. Duplicate for each approach and compare the same brief, counting unit, evidence standard and review period. Nothing calculates automatically or is submitted.

For each input set status to known, estimate, unknown or not_applicable. Blank value or blank status means unknown, never zero. Enter 0 only for a confirmed zero. Use not_applicable only for a deliberately excluded item and explain why. For each result use complete, estimated, incomplete or not_applicable. Unknown applicable inputs leave the result blank and incomplete; do not silently sum only the known entries.

Enter person-hours, not elapsed calendar time. Add the time of everyone doing the task. Keep stages disjoint: initial checking goes in verification; independent QA goes in QA; corrections go in rework. Include time spent on held, rejected and duplicate candidates. Keep buyer briefing, review and handover effort even if someone else does the research.

Plain-text rule: stage person-hours = processed units x person-minutes per unit / 60 + one-off person-hours. Record your own processed count, timing basis and one-off effort in basis_or_notes. Counts differ by stage; do not use accepted count for every stage. Alternatively enter measured stage person-hours. Do not add both measured and estimated hours for the same work.
Describe your own in-house, licensed-platform, analyst-supported or hybrid workflow; no approach is assumed to win.

State required activity, territory, exclusions, acceptance checks and required fields. Keep this standard fixed when comparing approaches; note coverage differences rather than hiding them in a cost figure.
Choose company or facility and define its unique identity. Count several sites as one company when the unit is company. The same unit must be used in the target, reviewed batch and accepted output.

State the dates or duration covered, whether this is initial work or refresh, the cutoff for decisions and which tasks are included. Do not compare a one-off batch with a recurring service period without adjustment.
State whether a bounded signal search is required, the qualifying signal and its evidence/recency rules. Not assessed is different from no qualifying signal found; neither proves no project exists.
Your desired unique output count, not an assumed achievable yield. Leave unknown if undecided. Keep the target separate from reviewed and actually accepted counts.

Count all rows in this bounded batch, including duplicate rows and rows ending in hold or rejection. Assign each row exactly one final status below. For planned work mark estimates; do not present a target as an observed count.

Count only unique company or facility anchors meeting the brief at the cutoff. Exclude held, rejected and duplicate rows. This is the denominator for the optional per-accepted-unit results, not proof of a sales opportunity.
Count unresolved rows at the same cutoff; do not treat missing evidence as acceptance. Use mutually exclusive final statuses so no row also appears as accepted, rejected or duplicate.
Count rows ending in rejection against this brief. Do not count them again as held or duplicate.
Count extra rows resolved to another anchor under your counting rule. Retain useful site detail without counting it as another company. Unresolved duplicate candidates stay held until resolved.
Record buyer time defining criteria, aligning reviewers and briefing any external researcher. Include one-off setup only once.
Record time assessing relevant sources, access and permitted use. Time entered here does not establish that rights have been cleared.
Record searching, filtering or shortlisting time for all candidates processed, not only eventual accepted units.
Record first-pass identity, activity, location and exclusion checks plus initial evidence recording. Keep independent QA and later corrections in their own stages.
Record any separately required signal review, including searches yielding no qualifying signal. If not part of the brief mark not_applicable and explain; do not enter zero to mean not researched.
Record entity matching, duplicate resolution and final count reconciliation without re-entering verification time.
Record reviewer time checking evidence and acceptance decisions. Keep time spent correcting issues in rework, not both stages.
Record corrections, repeated checks and resolving review queries. Enter confirmed zero only if no such effort occurred; planned rework remains your own estimate or unknown.
Record time reviewing delivery, recording limitations and preparing the agreed internal handoff. This sheet does not authorise outreach.
Record only refresh effort not already included above. Mark not_applicable if refresh is outside the period; if its work is allocated to the earlier stages, explain and do not count it twice.

Optional: choose one currency or other monetary accounting unit and use it consistently. Do not combine currencies or money and time in a single cost total. Leave cost results not_applicable if you only need the effort view.

Optional: enter your own internal cost basis; no rate is supplied. If roles have different rates use your own effort-weighted rate and document the underlying hours and rates in basis_or_notes. Do not use an unweighted average. Unknown rate leaves labour cost unknown.

unit: cost units for this review period
plain_text_guidance: Optional: enter attributable non-labour internal costs, with allocation basis and inclusions in basis_or_notes. Exclude anything already covered by your hourly cost and do not enter an agency price here. This is not a complete supplier-price comparison. Enter confirmed zero only if none are included; unknown is not zero.

Plain-text rule: candidate rows reviewed - (accepted unique units + held rows + rejected rows + duplicate rows). Calculate only with every count known or estimated on the same basis; an explicit 0 means reconciled counts, not verified evidence quality. Resolve any nonzero difference before using per-unit results.

Plain-text rule: add all applicable Effort rows once. Confirm every stage as known, estimated or deliberately not_applicable. Leave blank and incomplete if any applicable stage is unknown; if any included input is estimated mark the result estimated. Excluded tasks are not claimed as zero workload.

Plain-text rule: total buyer effort / accepted unique units. Use only a reconciled batch and a positive accepted count. If accepted count is known zero leave this result blank and not_applicable; if unknown leave blank and incomplete. Include effort on unsuccessful candidates in total effort. This is not a productivity benchmark.

Plain-text rule: total buyer effort x own internal hourly cost. Person-hours x cost units per person-hour gives cost units. Use only matching workload and cost bases; leave blank if the rate or effort is unknown. Mark estimated if any contributing input is estimated.

Plain-text rule: selected internal labour cost + other selected internal costs. Both terms must use the same cost unit and review period without overlap. An excluded non-labour category can be omitted only with a documented not_applicable status; label the result labour-only. Unknown costs leave the result incomplete. This selected-cost total is not an agency quote, ROI or savings estimate.

field: Selected internal cost per accepted unit
plain_text_guidance: Plain-text rule: selected internal cost total / accepted unique units. Use only a reconciled batch and a positive accepted count. Known zero accepted units means not_applicable; unknown count means incomplete. Carry forward any estimate or labour-only limitation. Different evidence standards or excluded costs prevent a like-for-like conclusion.
